body: As usual, the answer depends on you and your financial circumstances—plus what you mean by “alternative investments.” The term casts a wide net, so let’s start there. **What Is an Alternative Investment?**. It might be easier to start by listing what are **NOT** usually thought of as alternative investments. If we consider everything else to be an alternative asset, that creates a huge, and ever-evolving range of possibilities—from hedge funds and private equity opportunities (including today’s blank-check SPACs), to cryptocurrency, artwork, commodities, real estate, and more. When evaluating whether to add alternative investments to your portfolio, it is important to consider your overall wealth and family goals. If there is a downturn in the market and the fund is weakened by it, the fund manager may impose lockup periods, when investors cannot make withdrawals or redeem their fund shares. If all of the above applies to you, there may be a place for alternative investments in your portfolio—if you’re making the right choices for the right reasons.

# The Pros and Cons of Alternative Investments. Investing in Alternative Assets: Pros and Cons. Alternative investments have been getting increased attention, but they typically involve higher risk, limited liquidity, and more complex fee structures. * Things to consider before investing in alternative investments. ## What are alternative investments? ## Pros and Cons of Alternative Assets. With some alternative investments, you may lose access to your money for years. Even if the alternative investment is packaged in a mutual fund wrapper, the fund may not have daily liquidity. A common selling point of alternatives such as venture capital and private equity is the ability to get in on the ground floor of the next great company. The right half of the chart shows returns for venture capital, private equity and hedge funds (all considered a form of alternative investment). It’s important to fully understand all fees associated with an alternative investment and how they will impact the investment's performance before committing to buy.
